scope: Final visible Draft, exact source/article/action/deployed-JSON bytes, generation and publication timing, DL-6 backup coverage and retention limits, open-PR inventory, Fleet Runner Git ancestry and qualification state, proposed ADR review ownership, review-data versus editorial authority, held action custody, and current review registry/discovery state. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The backup does not store every file
findings.location: Line 25 says each file is stored by its hash.
findings.explanation: The pinned backup contract excludes the credentials file, restore-drill scratch roots, and specified SQLite WAL, SHM, and journal files.
findings.correction: Say regular data-root content is stored by hash subject to the documented credential, scratch-root, and SQLite side-file exclusions.

findings.title: Pruning and the quick-check blind spot defeat the absolute recovery guarantee
findings.location: Line 25 calls every run append-only by default and says a bad run can never overwrite a good backup.
findings.explanation: Default keep-four retention prunes older snapshots and unreferenced bodies, while a same-size, same-mtime source change is not reread and can go unseen.
findings.correction: Say kept manifests and object bodies are not overwritten, while retention deletes aged snapshots and unreferenced bodies and the size/mtime quick check has a documented blind spot. Do not promise that bad runs can never age out the last good snapshot.

findings.title: The open-PR inventory is fifteen Draft and nine non-Draft PRs
findings.location: The summary and lines 11 and 49 report twelve open Draft PRs and one open regular PR across core and BookcaseDiscovery.
findings.explanation: At review time GitHub listed eight Draft and eight non-Draft PRs in core plus seven Draft and one non-Draft PR in BookcaseDiscovery; every counted PR predated the article source revision.
findings.correction: Report fifteen Draft and nine non-Draft open PRs, or name a narrower filter and count only PRs that satisfy it.

findings.title: The NAS work is not one six-hop strict merge chain
findings.location: Lines 37 and 57–66 call #584 the base, put #589 directly on #586, call #591 independent of input delivery, and put #90 behind #584 and #586.
findings.explanation: Core #584 is stacked on #579 through #583, #589 is based on #588, and #591 is based on #589. BookcaseDiscovery #90 is based on #53 and vendors a pinned core client, while #91 and #92 form a separate application stack.
findings.correction: Show the full core stack, the separate BookcaseDiscovery stack, and the pinned vendoring and qualification relationship between them instead of one six-hop merge order.

findings.title: Downstream implementation and qualification already proceeded
findings.location: Lines 53 and 59–64 say #584 and #586 must land before any downstream NAS work can proceed and that they gate everything downstream.
findings.explanation: Core #588, #589, and #591 record completed G3, automatic-input, and observer/control qualification. BookcaseDiscovery #90, #91, and #92 record real two-Mac input, policy/resource, presence, and control proofs on exact stacked or vendored revisions.
findings.correction: Distinguish merge ancestry from work progress: the stack is unmerged, but downstream implementation and bounded qualification have already proceeded.

findings.title: Core #590 names its reviewer and acceptance gate
findings.location: Line 80 and retained context line 104 say the Proposed ADR has no stated reviewer or disposition.
findings.explanation: Core #590 explicitly leaves Owner review unchecked, says numbering and glossary adoption follow acceptance, and lists six open questions. The implementation PRs reviewed here do not declare accepted #590 as their merge prerequisite.
findings.correction: Report owner review and the six open questions as the ADR's documented gate; do not say the reviewer is unstated or invent ADR acceptance as a prerequisite for unrelated stacked PRs.

findings.title: Review-data PRs are advisory records, not the article-correction path
findings.location: Line 84 says the five Draft review PRs are accuracy-closure obligations and that the correction path runs through them.
findings.explanation: The pinned method and discovery service keep independent review data and correspondence separate from article revision, acceptance, readiness, and merge. The prior day's exact-source review PR states the same boundary.
findings.correction: Describe them as Draft review-data proposals with open findings awaiting supervised editorial disposition, and route article correction through the separate editorial revision flow.

findings.title: The three held lookups ask for states already present in primary sources
findings.location: Lines 53, 59–60, 91, and 101–105 call #584, #586, and BookcaseDiscovery #40 uncharacterized and propose status lookups.
findings.explanation: Core #584 is an open Draft based on #583's head; #586 is an open Draft with recorded G0–G2 receipts, later stacked work, and an explicit no-merge-request limit; BookcaseDiscovery #40 is an open Draft with recorded live two-host acceptance.
findings.correction: Preserve the candidate IDs but mark the lookup premises invalid or superseded in supervised action review; if follow-up remains useful, ask for the owner's actual disposition of the full stacks.
